description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 commit d68b4e3 ("close blocked-sender suppression gaps for typing/presence").

Spec text: "The server MUST check whether the requesting account corresponds to a ChatContact whose blocked: true on the recipient's contact list; if so, MUST silently drop for that recipient. Sender not informed. Per-recipient (not per-call) check." Applies to:
- Chat/typing handler (this bead)
- Push typing event (transport-layer; out of kit scope but the predicate is the hook)
- Push presence event (same)

Current state: ChatContact has a `blocked: bool` field but there is no ChatBackend hook to query it on the typing fan-out path. handle_chat_typing in chat-server/src/chat.rs has no blocked-check.

## Acceptance — kit side only (enforcement is impl's job)

- New ChatBackend method:
  ```rust
  fn is_contact_blocked(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &Id,
      _contact_id: &Id,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send {
      // Default: not blocked. Reference MemoryBackend overrides to consult ChatContact.blocked.
      async { Ok(false) }
  }
  ```
- handle_chat_typing in chat-server/src/chat.rs consults is_contact_blocked for the requesting caller's identity vs. each direct-chat recipient (group/channel: skip blocked-check since per-recipient fan-out is out-of-kit-scope, see "Notes")
- For direct chats: the recipient is derivable from Chat.contact_id; the handler calls is_contact_blocked(caller, account_id, contact_id). If true, handler returns the spec-required "success" response (echo accountId) WITHOUT calling whatever notification path the consumer plugged in.
- MemoryBackend (feature = "memory") implements is_contact_blocked by reading ChatContact.blocked
- Test (uses MemoryBackend): owner has ChatContact { contact_id: X, blocked: true }. owner sends Chat/typing for direct chat with X. Handler returns success but a Tracking helper observes no notification call. [This may require a new test-only TrackingBackend or use of the existing TrackingBackend if present.]

## Notes

The kit does NOT implement typing fan-out. It is a handler-library; transport (SSE/WS push of typing events) lives in the consumer. So "silently drop for that recipient" is enforced by:
1. Kit handler returns success
2. Kit handler does NOT call any push-notification hook (because there isn't one in the kit)
3. Consumer's typing-event publisher MUST consult is_contact_blocked before fanning out (consumer's responsibility, but the predicate is provided)

For group/channel chats (n recipients), per-recipient suppression is entirely the consumer's transport-layer job — the handler has no way to enumerate recipients. The kit hook supports it; the kit handler doesn't drive it.

Add a doc-comment on handle_chat_typing explaining this contract.

## Out of scope

- Push presence-event suppression (transport-layer; consumer integrates)
- Federation Peer/typing suppression (Layer E federation work)
title: Layer B: ChatBackend::is_contact_blocked + Chat/typing handler integration
